title: Rifts
dek: Tears into Fenumion from elsewhere, opened for things being summoned or trying to escape.

facts.Passage: Summoning or attempted escape from elsewhere

body:
A rift is an extra-dimensional tear into Fenumion from another place. It can open for something being summoned, or for something trying to escape. The tear is the connection; it is not the name of a single destination or plane.

What lies beyond can differ radically from one opening to another. Adventurers describe dreamlike spaces, clockwork passages, magical ooze, black-stone expanses, volcanic terrain and a contested shore. These encounters do not establish one shared “rift plane,” one creator, or one purpose behind every breach.

A breach in the boundary

A rift allows places normally separated from Fenumion to come into contact with it. That contact may involve a summons, an escape attempt, creatures, hostile influence or people crossing to investigate. An opening can be conspicuous across great distances, and accounts describe travelers entering from different parts of the world and meeting in the same encounter.

Entry is often a deliberate choice, but it is not universally voluntary. An earlier quest describes a collapsing rift exerting a violent pull and dragging participants into it. Nor is every unusual passage a rift: another quest explicitly distinguishes a realm-between-realms encounter from one.

What experience establishes

The environment itself can be dangerous. Unfamiliar space, dreamlike perceptions, heat, hostile creatures and unstable boundaries may matter as much as the immediate opponent. A vision or a creature’s explanation remains something a traveler experienced or heard; it does not automatically settle the cosmology of the place.

Rift expeditions can fail. The dreamlike breach’s closing narration describes an overwhelmed party retreating without fully sealing it, with narration warning of ripples and nightmares afterward. Defeating the enemies within reach also need not destroy the greater threat beyond: the ooze account ends with a vastly larger creature still visible as the opening closes.

Read the ooze expedition’s changing fight →

Retreat and return

Cecil’s post in the clockwork encounter includes an instruction allowing a participant to spend an action to leave while the breach remains open. That is a recorded permission in that encounter, not an unconditional escape action guaranteed in every rift. Incapacitation, hostile forces and collapse can prevent a retreat.

Repeated accounts describe survivors returning toward their entry locations when a rift closes. The volcanic account places Farkur back in Pristinia and Djöhandrai back on the trail between Gartina’s estate and the town, despite his attempt to follow another traveler. An earlier quest likewise narrates participants returning to where they answered the call.

These outcomes establish a recurring pattern, not a promise of safe return. They also give no general entitlement to use a closing rift as transport to another adventurer’s home. The outcome and permissions of the particular quest govern what actually happens.

Read the dream expedition’s failed sealing and retreat →

Read the coastal company’s battle and care after the fighting →

Objects and rewards

The Writer explicitly rules that objects from rifts cannot ordinarily be taken out as loot. A character’s plan to harvest a crystal, collect components or take alien machinery does not establish that the attempt succeeds. Later scenes also explicitly allow time for harvesting, including the abyssal and coastal endings. These permissions must be read alongside the separate restriction on carrying things across planes; time to harvest is not by itself proof that every collected object can be taken home. A specific reward or transport exception requires its own ruling.

Interacting with something inside a rift is distinct from carrying it home. Studying, moving, destroying or using an object during an encounter does not by itself establish that it can survive passage into Fenumion.

What holds a breach open?

Some accounts connect the opening’s stability to a creature, ritual, structure or concentrated source of energy. In the volcanic account, destruction of a central crystal is followed immediately by the dimension tearing and the rift beginning to close. The planned-breach account describes ritual sigils and notes about a weak boundary, alignment and sustaining the opening.

Those are useful observations for those encounters. They do not prove that every rift contains an anchor, that every crystal has the same function, or that destroying the largest visible object will close a breach. Some openings have no identified architect; evidence of deliberate intervention in one does not supply the cause of another.

Read the altar, map and planned breach →

Read the struggle to destroy the volcanic crystal →

Related histories remain distinct

Elenia reports that the western green mist came through a rift and distinguishes it from the Pale Man’s Haze. That testimony does not resolve the connection among the mist, the breach and Abyss. The new encounter summaries do not supply that missing cause. The October Babel expedition adds observed lures, altered perception, paralysis and a temporary clearing; those results still do not establish the rift’s cause or closure.

Pappy’s ambush and Adelia’s rescue remain established events in their own records. The primary rift transcript places Pappy’s peril and extraction within the same 3 September encounter as Cthulhu’s arrival. Pappy is pulled out before the god crosses. This establishes the event sequence without resolving the later dispute about knowledge and intervention.

What remains unresolved

The underlying boundary, the causes of recurrence, the identity of particular summoners, the full limits on permanent passage and the fate of an unsealed breach require evidence from their own scenes. The user-established definition permits things to be summoned or to seek escape through a rift; it does not make every attempt successful or settle every creature’s motive.

Recognizing a familiar kind of danger is useful. Assuming that the next opening must follow the last encounter’s rules is not knowledge of what lies beyond it.

Read what the moving heads revealed →

Rifts in recorded history

These encounters also appear in Events. Dates labeled “source posts” identify the surviving account. Cthulhu’s arrival is confirmed as 3 September 2026; the final posts fall on 4 September UTC, still 3 September EDT. Select an event for its outcome and evidence.

  1. Source posts · 31 March 2025 · in-world date unresolvedA dreamlike rift remains unsealedArjahn, Harry, Lucido, Yllandaer, Magnus and Dez face a living dream feeding on a dead titan’s weapon. Harry is crushed, nightmares overwhelm the company, and the retreat leaves the breach unsealed.Rift expedition fails · Read the full story →
  2. Source posts · 1–2 April 2025 · in-world date unresolvedA clockwork rift opens into hostile machineryTravelers enter clockwork passages with hostile machinery. Cecil’s post includes the action-to-leave instruction; later, Carmen carries an unconscious companion out as others retreat.Rift expedition · Read the full story →
  3. Source posts · 17–18 April 2025 · in-world date unresolvedAn ooze rift closes with a larger threat beyondNimueh’s lightning divides an ooze, and the black creatures recover in their own slime. The party defeats the immediate attackers, glimpses a castle-sized ooze beyond the closing breach, and exchanges tuning forks before being pulled home.Rift closure · Read the full story →
  4. Source posts · 17 July 2026 · in-world date unresolvedRitual evidence reveals a sustained breachScribonia’s meteor strike destabilizes the watching eye. After the enemies fall, investigators find an altar and map establishing that this breach was planned, then take separate tears out of the collapsing space.Rift investigation · Read the full story →
  5. Source posts · 7 August 2026 · in-world date unresolvedA vast rift leads into a dark expanseA battle among moving giants leaves severed heads trying to restore their bodies. Oscar’s investigation reveals the danger; Scribonia proposes destroying the heads, and the narrator assumes everyone escapes before closure.Rift expedition · Read the full story →
  6. Source posts · 3–4 September 2026 · in-world date unresolvedAn abyssal rift becomes a crisis of allegianceAn abyssal encounter becomes a contested summoning: creatures gnaw at the boundary while a robed figure coaxes a godlike form through. Pappy is attacked, offered an exit, and later pulled out. The remaining creatures complete the crossing immediately afterward.Rift encounter · Read the full story →
  7. 3 September 2026 · date confirmed by the world’s creatorCthulhu comes through a rift into FenumionCthulhu, the eldritch god, comes through the abyssal rift after creatures finish tearing at the boundary. Pappy has just been pulled out. As the space contracts, Cthulhu devours the creatures that freed him and departs to serve a master.Extra-dimensional arrival · Read the full story →
  8. Source posts · 25 September 2026 · in-world date unresolvedA volcanic rift collapses after its crystal is destroyedFenwick, Espera, Scribonia, Djöhandrai, Farkur and Ryvyt fight through lava and falling rock. Farkur attacks the renewing crystal as companions restore the fallen; its destruction tears the dimension and forces separate returns.Rift closure · Read the full story →
  9. Source posts · 8 October 2026 · in-world date unresolvedA coastal rift opens onto a battle from the seaNymera holds the shore for Fenwick, Vessalia, Di’trillio and Ryvyt as successive goblin waves arrive. Fenwick brings down meteors and banishes the final three; Vessalia insists the wounded Nymera deserves healing before the company returns.Rift encounter · Read the full story →
  10. 31 October–1 November 2026 · one continuous encounterThe Eversong masquerade turns the travelers’ shadows against themMusic and masks give way to hostile shadows. Scribonia brings Estella down while Aravil and Pin fight through failing sight; the rift contracts and sealing begins.Rift encounter · Read the full story →

A masquerade that turns on its guests

The Eversong encounter begins with music, masks and a promise of hospitality. The company’s shadows become hostile, and several travelers fight without sight. Scribonia’s final lightning brings Estella down; afterward the rift contracts and he begins to seal it.

The scene records that contraction, Aravil’s recovered sight and the start of sealing. The source does not separately show every traveler back at their starting point. Read the full Eversong story.
